record.title: The Glass Eye
record.premise: The order's new Voh-Vastei finds the "Eye of Argonia" sold in Gideon is glass, takes its old silver setting from the smugglers of the South Watch, and brings it to Nesh-Deeka, who reads the ship's name scratched inside it.
record.foundation: Built from main-plot.md §5 quest 6, as passed by the owner. Kept: the glass Eye in Gideon's market, the dealer who admits it for a few coins or a little Speech, the smugglers of the South Watch who kept the old silver setting in a locked chest in the ruin's inner room (Old Laboratory's one interior), the Collector's courteous note in the chest, the ship's name scratched inside the setting and Nesh-Deeka's reading of it. Filled from the plot and the lore, smallest reading first: the dealer's name (Ovinius Calo, a Nibenese-descended trader of Gideon); a third way to the dealer's fact (his note from the South Watch, carried, to pickpocket or take from his body); the lock's level (Apprentice) and the key on the smugglers' boss; the Unbound's visit to Gideon's market that Nesh-Deeka already knows of.

truth.what: The Pale Harvest, a Company freighter, sank with a Gideon dealer's whole stock aboard; an old silver setting with no stone, its ship's name scratched inside, was among it.
Salvagers sold the setting to the smugglers; the smugglers put a garnet of green-red glass in it and sold the glass alone to Ovinius Calo as the Eye of Argonia, keeping the silver to melt.
Two Unbound asked after the Eye at Ovinius's stall and went away when they saw it was glass.
The Collector, Ennodius Vanin, slipped into the inner room, opened the chest, found the setting of no use to him and left a note for whoever came next.

facts.claim: The Eye of Argonia on Ovinius Calo's stall is glass.
Ovinius bought the glass from the smugglers of the South Watch, who kept the old silver setting it came in.
Ennodius Vanin, the Collector, an Imperial relic-hunter, has hunted the Eye for twenty years and got to the chest first.
The name scratched inside the setting is the Pale Harvest, a ship that sank in Hatandros Bight with a Gideon dealer's whole stock aboard.
Two Unbound asked after the Eye in Gideon's market a month ago.

topics.label: I need the rootworm to Gideon.
topics.intent: Cheeval-Xu, at the landing under Helstrom's tree. Tells: the rootworm runs through the roots to Gideon's Hist garden; 25 gold. Checks: nothing (the fare is the travel network's). Does: nothing.

topics.label: You are selling the Eye of Argonia?
topics.intent: Ovinius Calo. Tells: it is the Eye of the old priest-kings, lost for ages, and the price is three thousand gold; he will not say where he got it. The player can press him (Persuade), pay him 20 gold for the truth, or let it be. Checks: nothing. Does: nothing.

topics.label: (Persuade) Nobody pays three thousand for glass. Tell me where it came from.
topics.intent: Ovinius. Tells: it is glass, a garnet of the cheap kind; he bought it from the smugglers of Gideon South Watch, the leaning Imperial tower south-east of the quay; they kept the old silver setting it came in, to melt. Two Unbound came asking after it a month ago and went away when they saw it was glass. A man called the Collector asked too. Does: sets stage 20.
topics.fallback: He is an honest dealer and the price is the price; for twenty gold he might remember more.

topics.label: Here is something for your memory. (20 gold)
topics.intent: Ovinius. Takes 20 gold. Tells: all that topic.mn06-persuade tells. Does: sets stage 20.

topics.label: Who are you?
topics.intent: Ovinius Calo, a dealer in old things at his stall on Blackwood Way; his family came from the Nibenay two hundred years ago. Does: nothing.

topics.label: Who is the Collector?
topics.intent: Ovinius. Tells: Ennodius Vanin, an Imperial relic-hunter who has chased the Eye of Argonia for twenty years; courteous, rich, and he tells what he learns to whoever pays him. He passed through Gideon a few days ago. Does: nothing.

topics.label: What is Gideon South Watch?
topics.intent: Ovinius. Tells: an Imperial watch-tower that leans on the mud south-east of the quay; the delta smugglers moor under it and shoot at anyone on the pier; their boss keeps to the top. Does: nothing.

topics.label: What is Gideon?
topics.intent: Ovinius. Tells: the frontier city of the Blackwood Road; its council sits in the old Governor's Mansion and denies the Xeech-Leel's claim; it trades with Leyawiin. Does: nothing.

topics.label: Here is the setting the glass Eye came in.
topics.intent: Nesh-Deeka. Tells: she turns it to the light and reads the name scratched inside: the Pale Harvest. She knows it: a Company freighter that sank in Hatandros Bight with a Gideon dealer's whole stock aboard. Then she says the Unbound were in Gideon's market a month ago, two of them, asking after that same glass. Does: nothing (a question; its answer is topic.mn06-how-know).

topics.label: How do you know the Unbound were in Gideon?
topics.intent: Nesh-Deeka. Tells: "We listen." She turns to the wreck, pays 100 gold and gives the setting back. Does: sets stage 90.

topics.label: How do you always know where the Unbound have been?
topics.intent: Nesh-Deeka. Tells: "We listen, and the marsh talks." She will say no more and asks about the player's road. Open in every later report window of Act II. Does: nothing.

know_text:
My notes so far. I came up the river on an Owing barge to cut reed at Ashgate Landing (the Owing is the marsh's sentence: months of owed work instead of a cell), but my name was struck off the gang's roll on an order from Vosh-Leera, the root-herald of Jal-Veesa. She works for the Toh-Reel-Ka, the "Secret Warriors" of the Xeech-Leel, who rule Black Marsh. The order was made after Umbriel, when the An-Xileel used Lilmoth's mad Hist to call a flying city down on the marsh; it exists so no tree, and no one allied with a tree, can do that again. They recruit strangers with no ties like me because we are useful and cheap.

A Hist is a huge grey tree that every Argonian village is built round; its eggs lie in a pool at its foot and its sap shapes hatchlings and brings visions. Trees are falling sick: the scar where the minder draws sap closes, the bark darkens, the egg-pool cools. Jal-Veesa's tree is sick. I drank a cup of sap and had a vision that led me to Teel-Fen Weir, where the young tree's scar was sealed with a grey paste, and to a hide where three of the Unbound (a cult of tribeless Argonians who drain sap) kept jars of sap. Their note sent me to Karsh-Naal Camp, where I freed Sesk, a Naga who drew sap for them. She named their leader, Cuts-the-Old-Knot, said the sap is for a draught to do with "the Eye", and called the grey paste "the seal".

Vosh-Leera sent me by the rootworm to the order's handler, Nesh-Deeka, in her house in Helstrom. I got a jar of stolen sap off an Unbound go-between there and she made me a Voh-Vastei, the order's first rank (I got light armour and 200 gold). She told me the Eye of Argonia is the old priest-kings' jewel, cut from Hist amber, lying at the Root (where all the trees' roots meet, under the sea) behind a gate the old kings sealed; used there it could heal every tree. We think Cuts-the-Old-Knot's draught is to kill whatever guards the Root. The order wants me to find the Root first and use the Eye where it sits. Her one lead: an "Eye of Argonia" is for sale in Gideon. The rootworm goes there from Helstrom's city tree. I'm to go to Gideon.
